name: Chicago Architecture Boat Tour
unique: Ninety minutes up the Chicago River while a docent explains how the city invented the skyscraper, with the river canyon as the classroom.
buzz: The Architecture Center's tour is the one locals recommend; sunset departures are the best. Book ahead in summer.

name: Art Institute of Chicago
unique: Nighthawks, American Gothic, a room of Thorne miniatures and the best Impressionist collection outside Paris, behind a bronze lion on Michigan Avenue.
buzz: The miniatures and the modern wing are the sleeper hits; go on a weekday morning and pick two wings.

name: Field Museum
unique: A natural history museum with SUE the T. rex, ancient Egyptian tombs, a man eating lion exhibit and a vast Native American collection.
buzz: The dinosaur and the Egypt gallery are the priorities, and the building itself is grand. Allow half a day.

name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
unique: Wright's own home and studio, where he developed the Prairie style, with guided tours and a neighborhood full of his houses.
buzz: The studio tour is the best architecture hour in the Chicago area. Book ahead and walk the neighborhood after.

name: Museum of Science and Industry
unique: A huge science museum with a real U-boat, a coal mine, a 727 and a giant model train layout, in the 1893 World's Fair building.
buzz: The U-boat tour is the standout and the coal mine is a close second. Plan for half a day.

name: Second City
unique: The cabaret theater that launched Belushi, Fey and Colbert, still running improvised and scripted shows with a live band and a cheap bar.
buzz: The mainstage shows are consistently sharp; the improv sets are hit or miss and cheaper. Sit close and expect to be teased.

name: Cahokia Mounds
unique: The largest pre Columbian city north of Mexico, with 120 mounds including Monks Mound, bigger at its base than the Great Pyramid, and a solar calendar of posts.
buzz: The museum is excellent and the climb is easy; sunset from Monks Mound is the move. Quiet and little visited.

name: Galloping Ghost Arcade
unique: More than eight hundred playable arcade machines, all on free play for one flat fee, from 1970s black and white cabinets to prototypes that never shipped.
buzz: The collection is absurd and the owner is usually on the floor fixing something. Weeknights are quiet and weekends are a tournament scene.

name: Shedd Aquarium
unique: A 1930 aquarium on the lake with a Caribbean reef, belugas, otters and a Amazon flooded forest, plus a aquatic show.
buzz: The beluga and otter habitats are the favorites, and the building is beautiful. Book tickets ahead.

name: Wrigley Field
unique: The second oldest ballpark in the majors, with the ivy covered walls, the manual scoreboard and the rooftop seats across the street.
buzz: The tour gets you into the dugout and the press box, and the history is the draw. Book ahead.

name: Anderson Japanese Gardens
unique: Twelve acres of pond, stream and strolling garden designed by a Japanese master gardener, with a tea house and a waterfall.
buzz: Gardeners call it the best Japanese garden in the midwest and the koi are the family draw; the spring and fall are the peak seasons.

name: Chicago Riverwalk
unique: A 1.25 mile promenade along the Chicago River with bars, kayak rentals, architecture tours and the bridges overhead.
buzz: The river level view of the architecture is the reason, and the bars are a good stop. Best at sunset.

name: Galena Historic District
unique: A river town of brick storefronts, steep streets and 19th century houses, once a lead mining boomtown and now a weekend getaway.
buzz: The main street is polished and the houses are beautiful. Busy in fall.

name: Lincoln Park Zoo
unique: A free zoo in the middle of the city with lions, apes, penguins and a farm, open every day of the year.
buzz: Free and genuinely good, which is rare for a city zoo. The penguin house is the kid favorite.

name: Starved Rock
unique: Eighteen sandstone canyons with waterfalls and a lodge on a bluff above the Illinois River, an hour and a half from Chicago.
buzz: The canyons are beautiful and busy; go at 8am and take Trail 2. Bald eagles winter below the dam.

name: Garden of the Gods
unique: Weird sandstone hoodoos, camel shaped formations and a slot canyon in the Shawnee Hills, with a trail that threads between the rocks.
buzz: People call it a mini-Utah in southern Illinois; it is free and rarely crowded. Combine with the wine trail.

name: Millennium Park
unique: A downtown park with Cloud Gate, the Pritzker Pavilion, a fountain and a garden, on the old rail yards.
buzz: The Bean is the photo and the park is a good walk. Free and central.

name: Pullman National Historical Park
unique: A planned industrial town built by the Pullman company, with the factory, the row houses and the story of the 1894 strike.
buzz: The architecture and the labor history together are the point. Free, with a visitor center.

name: The Chopping Block
unique: A cooking school and shop where you make a full menu in a small group, from knife skills to braising, then sit down and eat it with the class.
buzz: The teaching is practical and the groups are friendly; date night classes book out.

name: Allerton Park
unique: A 1,500 acre estate with a formal garden, a brick-walled mansion and sculptures in the woods including the Fu Dog Garden.
buzz: The Fu Dog Garden and the sunken garden are the surprises and it is free; the park is between Champaign and Decatur and easy to miss.

name: Superdawg
unique: A drive in with two giant hot dog statues on the roof, carhops on rollerskates and a Chicago style dog with a pickled tomato, unchanged since 1948.
buzz: The nostalgia is the meal and the dogs are good; eat in the car or at the picnic tables. A classic.

name: Illinois State Fair
unique: A giant state fair with a butter cow, harness racing, a mile long midway and the Illinois Pork Producers' pork chop on a stick.
buzz: It is the platonic state fair; the butter cow is a genuine attraction. Parking and heat are the usual complaints.

name: Caterpillar Visitors Center
unique: A visitor center with a 797 mining truck, a simulator and the story of the tractors that changed farming, in the company's hometown.
buzz: The big machines and the simulator are the family draw and the history of the company is the adult part; it is indoors and cheap.

name: Krannert Art Museum
unique: A university museum with a strong collection of European painting, African art and contemporary work, free to the public.
buzz: The permanent collection is better than expected and the shows rotate often; it is free and the café is a campus meeting spot.

name: Burpee Museum of Natural History
unique: A natural history museum with Jane, a juvenile T. rex, and a working paleontology lab, on the Rock River.
buzz: Jane is the reason children ask to come and the lab is where visitors can watch preparation; the museum is small and cheap.

name: Japan House
unique: A Japanese house and tea garden on the university campus, used for tea ceremonies and open to walk through.
buzz: The garden is the quiet corner of campus and the tea ceremonies need booking; it is free and small.

name: Peoria Riverfront Museum
unique: A combined art, history and science museum on the Illinois River with a giant screen theater and a dome planetarium.
buzz: The riverfront view and the planetarium are the reasons to go and the galleries are small; the museum is good with children on a rainy day.

name: Villa Kathrine
unique: A Moorish revival villa on the bluffs above the Mississippi, built by a wealthy traveler who never lived in it, with a courtyard and a view of the river.
buzz: The house is strange and photogenic and the river view is the reason to climb the hill; the tour is short and the restoration is ongoing.

name: Beer Nuts Factory
unique: The factory store where the sweet and salty peanuts have been made since 1937, with a window into the roasting room and a wall of merchandise.
buzz: The smell is the attraction and the store sells warm samples; it is a quick stop and the brand is a central Illinois institution.

name: Miller Park Zoo
unique: A small zoo in a city park with a rainforest building, a carousel and river otters, old enough to have been a city fixture since 1890.
buzz: Parents say it is the right size for toddlers and the rainforest building is the winter stop; it is cheap and never crowded.
